author: Copilot
body:
The inline rationale says using WARNING here would “create a new Sentry event on every hit”, but the repo’s Sentry LoggingIntegration is configured with event_level=ERROR, so WARNING logs should be breadcrumbs (not new events). Please update the comment (and/or the log-level choice rationale) to match the actual Sentry configuration, or reference the specific configuration path where WARNING is promoted to events if that’s the case in some environments.
```suggestion
        # Guard against pathologically deep structures. Log at DEBUG only to avoid high-volume
        # noise; with the current Sentry LoggingIntegration configuration, WARNING logs would
        # normally be captured as breadcrumbs rather than standalone Sentry events.
```

author: Copilot
body: The guard uses `if depth > self._MAX_SCRUB_DEPTH`, which means recursion will still proceed at `depth == _MAX_SCRUB_DEPTH` and only stops at `_MAX_SCRUB_DEPTH + 1`. If `_MAX_SCRUB_DEPTH` is meant to be a strict/inclusive maximum, consider switching to `>=` or clarifying the constant/comment to avoid off-by-one ambiguity.

author: Copilot
body: This change alters the max-depth behavior of `_deep_scrub` (new limit constant, different log level, and no longer replacing deep values). There are existing unit tests for PortalScrubber, but none appear to cover the depth-guard behavior. Please add a focused test that builds a nested dict/list beyond `_MAX_SCRUB_DEPTH` and asserts (1) no RecursionError, (2) scrubbing still happens up to the limit, and (3) the deep portion is left unchanged (no placeholder replacement).

author: Copilot
body: The depth-guard path calls `len(obj)` before the type sanity-check below. If `_deep_scrub` is ever invoked with a non-sized / non-(dict|list) object, this will raise (TypeError) before the early return can protect it. Consider moving the `isinstance(obj, dict | list)` check above the depth guard, or computing `len` only for dict/list.
